newsitem.title: CANADA: Sask Wheat Pool expanding beyond Canada.
newsitem.headline: Sask Wheat Pool expanding beyond Canada.

text.p: The head of Canada's largest grain handler on Tuesday said the firm is expanding its oilseed, grain and livestock processing businesses and in some cases, is reaching beyond Canada's borders to do it.
"Saskatchewan Wheat Pool's in a growth mode. We're continuing to build facilities in western Canada," SWP chief executive Don Loewen told Reuters in an interview.
Loewen said SWP is also establishing interests in Mexico, the United States and Poland.

"The only canola crushing plant we haven't expanded is Fort Saskatchewan (Alberta) and we'll look at that. We've been expanding our refineries as well and we'll probably build another refinery or two," Loewen said.
SWP is part owner of crusher CanAmera Foods.
CanAmera's plants in Nipawin, Sask., Harrowby and Altona, Man., and Hamilton, Ont., underwent expansions recently.
"We just closed the deal in Manzanillo (Mexico) to build a terminal there and we're continuing to press on all fronts, our hog initiative is going strong and hard," Loewen said.
Construction of the Manzanillo terminal was estimated at US$27 million. The facility will handle wheat, canola, corn, soybeans, sorghum and sunflower seeds.
SWP bought 35 percent of western Canadian pork packer Fletcher's Fine Foods Ltd on February 10 which began a C$20 million expansion of its Red Deer, Alberta, facility.
Once completed, the plant will process 8,000 hogs each shift compared to 4,000 now, he said.
Financing for an export terminal in Gdansk, Poland, in which SWP holds a 10 percent share should be in place by November, Loewen added.
The firm also paid C$14 million to raise its share in Can-Oat Milling and is building a mill near Saskatoon, Sask., which should produce 72,000 tonnes of milled oats a year.
On top of the 22 grain elevators SWP plans to build across western Canada in the next three years, the firm is building an elevator with General Mills Inc in North Dakota.

The 73-year-old cooperative has grown from a farmer-owned grain handling company with 440 elevators into a grain firm with holdings in processing facilities and off-shore export terminals since it issued shares on April 1, 1996.

SWP was added to the Toronto Stock Exchange 300 Composite Index of leading firms on February 21 and about half of its B-class shares are now held by farmers with the rest widely distributed, Loewen said.
The share offer and issuing a C$300 million medium-term note June 26 propelled SWP on its capital expansion, he added.

SWP posted sales of C$4 billion in the 1995/96 (Aug/July) crop year. Sales in the first nine months of 1996/97 were C$2.82 billion versus C$2.79 billion in the same time in the prior year. Year end figures were not available, Loewen said.
